concepts.def: Artwork made for and shaped by a specific space.
Pouring material into a mould to copy a form.
Negative shape used to cast a positive copy.
Shaping soft material like clay by hand.
Joining rigid parts into a sculpture.
Size relationship between artwork and viewer.

walkthroughs.body_html: An installation uses a whole room or site as its medium. Cornelia Parker's Cold Dark Matter suspends fragments of an exploded shed. The viewer walks around or through the piece — sightlines, shadows and even sound become design choices.

Casting begins with a positive (your model), takes a negative mould (silicone or plaster), then pours a new positive in metal, resin or plaster. Multiple casts can be made — that is why many famous bronzes exist in editions.

Antony Gormley's Angel of the North stands 20 metres tall with a 54-metre wingspan, dominating its hillside. A teaspoon-sized sculpture of the same figure would feel intimate, even fragile. Choose scale to match intent.
